name: rejection-safety
invariant: A parse that reports ok === false must not expose a field a consumer could mistake for a decision (target, recipient, functionName, params, amount, chainId, isTokenTransfer).
why: Consumers commonly branch on a field (`if (r.target) sendTo(r.target)`) instead of the status flag. If a rejected parse still carries a target, the consumer acts on an address the parser itself refused to accept -- e.g. a bad EIP-55 checksum.

cases.note: Mixed case is a checksum claim. This one is wrong. The address must not survive rejection.
Short address. If params survive, a token transfer builds against a truncated address.
Negative wei. Amount rejection must not leave the payee address usable.
Ambiguous between native and token units. A parser that rejects it must not also hand out a chosen number.

controlCases.note: A rejection-safety check must not be satisfiable by rejecting everything.
Positive control for the token path.
